# Benchmark sheet

<!-- Generated by demo/build_benchmark_sheet.py from benchmarks/baselines/2026-09-30-product/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every number below comes from one committed file, `benchmarks/baselines/2026-09-30-product/product_bench.json` (decision DM-2). Nothing is extrapolated, and every value is truncated, never rounded up. **These were not measured in Fabric**: live Fabric timings go in [`LIVE_TIMINGS.md`](LIVE_TIMINGS.md) after the owner's dry run.

## What was measured

- Machine: 4 cores, `Linux-6.18.44-fc-v50-x86_64-with-glibc2.39`, Python 3.11.15, started 2026-09-30 22:15:50.
- What ran: `shape.profile` itself, exact mode (the released behaviour), on the deterministic profiling datasets, written by `benchmarks/measure_product.py`.
- Each timing is the median of 3 runs, each in a fresh process. Wall-clock excludes `import shape`. Peak memory is the process's peak resident set size.
- Before any timing counts, the row count must match the file and the profile output must be identical across the runs (hash compared). Both held for every row below.

## Profiling: wall-clock, throughput and peak memory

| Dataset | Wall-clock s | Rows per second | Peak memory MB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| D1, 200k rows x 6 columns, Parquet | 0.38 | 519,131 | 224 |
| D2, 1M rows x 20 columns, Parquet | 1.96 | 509,495 | 638 |
| D2, 1M rows x 20 columns, CSV | 2.02 | 494,842 | 733 |
| D3, 5M rows x 10 columns, Parquet | 4.89 | 1,021,983 | 2,107 |
| D4, 100k rows x 200 columns, Parquet | 4.40 | 22,704 | 508 |

Rows per second is rows divided by the median wall-clock, truncated to a whole number.
Wide tables are slower per row: D4 has 200 columns.

## Start-up

Median of 7 fresh processes.

| What | Wall-clock ms |

| `python -c "import shape"` | 239 |
| `shape version` (the CLI) | 294 |
